module_title: Geographical Distribution and State-Specific Tribal Traits
introduction: This level maps specific tribes to their geographical regions. In competitive exams, 'Match the following' questions between a tribe and its state are the most common pattern. We also explore unique cultural nuances that distinguish these groups.

core_concepts.title: Central and Eastern Heartland
core_concepts.description: This region holds the largest tribal concentration. 1. Santhal & Munda: Primarily in 'Jharkhand', West Bengal, and Odisha. They are famous for historic rebellions (Santhal Rebellion of 1855). 2. Gond: Spread across Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Maharashtra.

core_concepts.title: Northeastern Tribes (Mongoloid Stocks)
core_concepts.description: 1. Garo, Khasi, Jaintia: Inhabiting the hills of 'Meghalaya'. 2. Bodo: The largest tribe in 'Assam'. 3. Naga: In Nagaland. 4. Kuki & Meitei: In 'Manipur' (highly relevant due to recent ethnic currents). 5. Lepcha & Bhutia: In 'Sikkim'.

core_concepts.title: Northern Nomads (Transhumance)
core_concepts.description: 1. Gaddi & Bakarwal: Nomadic pastoralists of 'Jammu & Kashmir' and 'Himachal Pradesh' who practice transhumance (seasonal migration with livestock). 2. Gujjar: Major pastoralist group across North India.

core_concepts.title: Southern Tribes
core_concepts.description: 1. Toda: Residing in the 'Nilgiri Hills' (Tamil Nadu), famous for their unique barrel-shaped huts and buffalo worship. 2. Chenchu: Primarily in 'Andhra Pradesh' and Telangana (Nallamala Hills).

important_entities.name: Tharu Tribe
important_entities.key_fact: Diwali as a Day of Mourning
important_entities.significance: Found in the 'Terai' region (India-Nepal border) of UP and Uttarakhand. Unlike most Indians, they traditionally observe Diwali as a day of mourning for their ancestors.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: The Garo, Khasi, and Jaintia Hills are named after the 'Tribes' that live there. It is not the other way around. These tribes follow a matrilineal system where lineage is traced through the mother.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Lepcha and Bhutia. Note: 'Bhutia' is from Sikkim, while 'Bhotia' is usually associated with Uttarakhand—do not confuse the two.

exam_strategy_tips: Rote memorize these specific pairings: Toda -> Nilgiris/Tamil Nadu; Lepcha -> Sikkim; Santhal -> Jharkhand; Bodo -> Assam.
The Kuki and Meitei tribes of Manipur are currently 'hot topics' for Current Affairs-based Geography questions.
